what_happened: After the job "hold and release for queued items" landed (about 10:10 UTC on 13 Nov), the drain rebuilt itself and continued. The new build still reported that it was built from a48031ceef1e, the old commit. It then refused to start with "stale build ... run ./setup.sh", and the batch stopped. The the person running Athena restarted the drain by hand. That restart rebuilt from a5f57002c326 and started cleanly. The batch was down until the restart.
cause: The in-process rebuild-and-continue step is not checked against the stale-build guard that runs next. Nothing confirms that the rebuilt binary embeds the new commit before the drain carries on. The step may not rebuild at all, or may rebuild without refreshing the embedded commit id (a build-cache or build-stamp problem). Either way, a drain that lands its own code change has no check that the build it continues with is current. The only recovery is a manual drain-restart, which does a full rebuild.
other_causes: The guard failed correctly and stopped the batch, but it has no recovery path. It does not retry the rebuild or re-exec, so a detectable fault becomes a stopped batch.
Related incidents on stale installed builds after self-landing were handled by manual setup re-runs, so the drain's self-rebuild path was never tested as a landing of its own code.
open_hypotheses: The rebuild step ran but the embedded commit id came from a stale build stamp or cache, so the binary is new but reports the old commit.
The rebuild step did not run, or built the wrong tree, before the drain re-executed.
The drain re-executed the old binary instead of the freshly built one.
The landing finished after the rebuild started, so the rebuild saw the pre-landing HEAD.
contradictions: No input fact points against the cause. The fields do not say why the build reported the old commit.
prevention: After the drain's self-rebuild, check that the new binary reports the commit now at HEAD before continuing. If it does not, redo the rebuild once, then re-exec into the new binary. If it still does not match, stop with a clear message. Add a test that lands a change to Athena's own code under a running drain and asserts that the drain continues on the new build. This applies to the whole class, not only this commit.
proposed_request: After the drain lands a job that changes Athena's own code, it rebuilds itself and continues. On 13 Nov it rebuilt but the new binary still reported the old commit a48031ceef1e, refused to start with "stale build ... run ./setup.sh", and the batch stopped. A manual drain-restart rebuilt from a5f57002c326 and started cleanly. Outcome: a drain that lands a change to Athena's own code carries on with a binary built from the commit now at HEAD, with no manual restart. Acceptance: (1) after the self-rebuild, the drain checks that the binary's embedded commit equals HEAD; on a mismatch it redoes the rebuild once and re-executes into the new binary, and if it still mismatches it stops with a message that names both commits. (2) A test lands a change to Athena's own code under a running drain, using a fake build whose first rebuild leaves a stale commit id, and shows that the drain recovers and continues. (3) A CHANGELOG.md entry is added.
